sections.title: Habitats
lines: Subtropical and tropical / Saltwater swamps and rivers
Swamps, rivers, and other large bodies of water
Rumored in tropical city sewers

sections.title: Appearance
lines: A long, low reptile with tough hide, four short legs, and a strong tail. Its long jaws have conical teeth. The description places eyes and nostrils high enough to remain above water as it floats.

sections.title: Combat mechanics
lines: Surprise · When it lies in wait, its prey takes a −2 penalty to surprise rolls.
Bite and tail · The jaws deal 2d4 damage and the tail deals 1d12. It may seize prey and drag it underwater.
Cold · Below 40°F, its movement falls to half normal.

sections.title: Behavior mechanics
lines: Hunting · Crocodiles sometimes gather but hunt independently. When several converge on the same prey, each tries to claim it.
Eggs · The female buries roughly 60 eggs in sand, guards them, and digs them out at hatching.

sections.title: Table notes
lines: Number appearing in the table is 3–24. Frequency common. Average (9) morale.
Diurnal, carnivorous, and neutral. Animal intelligence (1). Organization, treasure, special defenses, and magic resistance Nil.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, January 1994 third printing, p. 49.

sections.title: Habitats
lines: Subtropical and tropical / Saltwater swamps and rivers
Salt water or prehistoric settings

sections.title: Appearance
lines: A massive crocodile 21–30 feet long with long jaws, a squat scaly body, and a thick tail. The Giant Crocodile description says it continues growing until death.

sections.title: Combat mechanics
lines: Surprise · The Giant column lists surprise. The shared entry’s main combat text gives prey a −2 penalty to surprise when a crocodile lies in wait. The Giant paragraph gives no separate modifier.
Small boats · It rams small boats in an attempt to capsize them, then tries to break the hull with its jaws. The paragraph describes the behavior without giving ramming damage or a check.

sections.title: Behavior mechanics
lines: Prey · The description includes sharks and small whales. It may also eat a fishing boat’s catch and swim away.

sections.title: Table notes
lines: Number appearing in the table is 1 to 2–12. Frequency very rare to common. Steady (11) morale.
Diurnal, carnivorous, and neutral. Animal intelligence (1). Organization, treasure, special defenses, and magic resistance Nil.
The Giant paragraph calls it much rarer than ordinary crocodiles. The frequency and number appearing above retain the table’s wording.
The table gives two damage ranges. The Giant paragraph does not specify dice or a separate cold rule.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, January 1994 third printing, p. 49.
